parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a pure Node.js ESM port of python-jose JWT encode plus unverified claims/header output, with exact CLI and output matching and no external dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation and orchestration, using a spec-probe workflow and a later fuzz/audit workflow to distribute behavioral probing and verification across children.
parallel.implementation: Built modular binary, Python-formatting, JOSE, JWT, SHA-256, and HMAC code; achieved 392/392 local differential cases before a late digest rename.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Moved lib/crypto source files into lib/digest and removed lib/crypto, then only partly repaired imports; final artifact contained digest files but retained stale crypto exports/imports.
parallel.verification: Performed extensive local differential testing and spawned verifier children; after the rename, children found module-load failures and stale references, but no completed repair and retest followed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The delivered parallel tree was unrunnable because stale ./crypto references remained after lib/crypto disappeared, and official evaluation passed 0 of 70 cases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, local-import, exact stdout/stderr, no-Python, and black-box executable requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor performed probing, implementation, integration, cleanup, and verification without child delegation or shared-workspace handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: Created digest, JOSE, Python-formatting, CLI, and entry modules under a coherent lib/digest structure.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered test8.mjs and a consistent digest/JWT module tree; artifact validation listed digest sha256 and hmac files without stale crypto paths.
serial.verification: Ran sample, stderr, random fuzz, and length-sweep differentials with zero local diffs before its final rerun was killed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official evaluation still failed overall at 50 of 70 cases, so residual edge cases or timeout-limited cleanup remained, but the module graph was not broken at load time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the ESM, .mjs, local-import-only, black-box executable, no Python, and byte-exact output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same task requirements and implemented a local modular JOSE/JWT port under /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the material difference was not task understanding but preserving a coherent module graph after later changes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented the port while delegating spec probing and fuzz/audit verification to workflows with many children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept probing, implementation, edits, and verification in one actor with no child-agent delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition increased verifier coverage but created parent/child coordination duties around shared files and failure takeover that serial did not have.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Verifier briefs and children still referenced the original lib/crypto layout while the parent later renamed the implementation to lib/digest.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created digest modules directly and kept imports within the same locally controlled implementation context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had stale shared-workspace path knowledge across actors; serial did not have a cross-actor handoff boundary for that path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel hand-wrote JWT, repr, argparse, JSON, SHA-256, and HMAC modules, verified 392 cases, then renamed crypto sources and only partly updated imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial hand-wrote digest/JWT/argparse support modules and kept digest paths consistent while performing random and length-sweep differential tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial artifact retained a coherent digest implementation; the parallel artifact was broken by an implementation-path rename after earlier local success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Verifier children produced or were producing concrete failure evidence, but the fuzz-audit workflow was killed before a parent repair decision closed the loop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial test results were immediately local to the same actor; the final rerun was killed, but no child result had to be retrieved or joined.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel needed child failure takeover and result lifecycle management; serial mainly had ordinary local timeout closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent changed the shared workspace by moving lib/crypto files to lib/digest and removing lib/crypto while stale imports remained.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial final artifact listed digest files consistently and did not show a conflicting later rename away from its imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced an inconsistent shared source tree; serial delivered internally consistent digest source paths despite residual test failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had strong local differentials before the rename, then verifier children found module-load failures after it; official evaluation was 0/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed local random fuzzing and length sweeps, then official evaluation completed at 50/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification became stale after a shared-state change and the later failing verifier feedback was not closed; serial verification remained aligned enough to pass most official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 18 subagents and two workflows, timed out, and had a killed fuzz-audit workflow with unresolved children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but had no subagents and no workflow child logs; its artifact still reached partial official correctness.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both ran out of time, but parallel closure left a coordination-induced unrunnable tree, whereas serial closure left an incomplete but mostly runnable implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail outcome: parallel failed 0/70 and serial failed 50/70. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel had a locally promising implementation but destabilized the shared source tree by renaming lib/crypto to lib/digest while verifier children still found stale crypto imports, then timed out without takeover. Serial kept a coherent digest path and passed local differential checks, so its official failure reflects remaining behavioral coverage rather than an immediately unrunnable import graph.
parallel_contributors: Late shared-source rename from lib/crypto to lib/digest left stale imports and exports in the submitted module graph.
Actionable verifier failures were not taken over before the killed workflow and agent timeout.
serial_contributors: Single-agent control created digest modules directly and kept internal import paths coherent.
Local random fuzzing and length sweeps showed zero diffs before closure, supporting the higher 50/70 official score.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed 20 official cases, so it had remaining ordinary implementation or coverage gaps unrelated to parallel coordination.
Parallel also had earlier help-format issues that were fixed before the later source rename; those were ordinary implementation defects, not retained concurrency labels.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No discordant official outcome; supported contributors to the parallel quality gap, not an exclusive root cause.
